newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish T-bill auctions to continue - deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Turkish T-bill auctions to continue - deputy PM.

text.p: Turkey's government aimed eventually to eliminate domestic borrowing, and envisaged a balanced budget next year as a step towards that, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said.
She said however, it was impossible to stop Treasury bill auctions at present -- pouring cold water on a report that these were to end.

"Our aim is to remove domestic borrowing completely in time. A balanced 1997 budget target is a step towards this. But it is impossible to stop (t-bill) auctions at present," Ciller told a news conference on economic issues.
The mass circulation daily Hurriyet had reported the Treasury would stop auctioning Treasury bills, further fuelling T-bill demand on Tuesday in the bond market.
Bankers dismissed the report as unrealistic, but the news still buoyed already firm demand, causing yields in the most heavily traded 1997 maturity papers to fall by one to three points.
Yields firmed slightly after Ciller's comments.
Ciller said domestic borrowing would continue under what she called free market conditions and a balanced budget framework.
"We will see (domestic) borrowing decline slowly and gradually within market rules and the framework of a balanced budget," she added.
The 1997 budget, expected at around 7,000 trillion lira after 3,500 trillion in 1995, will be presented to parliament's budgetary commission by Thursday.
Ciller said it would be the first balanced budget in Turkey in decades.
-- Aydan Eksin, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875. EKS SY
